BACKGROUND AND SUMMARY
This application is a request for approval of a Site Plan and applicable deviations from
building design for approximately 2.75 acres located on the south side of 11400 S. and
west of State Street, at approximately 39 W. 11400 S. (Exhibit B & C). The property is
currently zoned CI. The applicant is requesting that a Site Plan and deviation requests be
approved to allow for the development of the currently vacant site with a 67’ 2” tall office
building. The application was submitted prior to a change in code and is allowed to apply
for a height deviation.

The property consists of three parcels that were sold to the current owner by the Utah
Department of Transportation (UDOT) as surplus property. An access easement extends
along the southernmost property boundaries that connects to State Street and provides
access to adjoining properties located south of the subject property.

The Community Commercial land use designation is characterized as follows:




According to Draper City Municipal Code (DCMC) Section 9-8-020 the purpose of the CI
zone is to “is to provide areas with visibility and access from Interstate 15 that are commuter
and traveler oriented. Typical uses include lodging facilities, personal services, travel plazas,
restaurants and fast food facilities, and commuter parking.”

Site Plan Layout. The proposed site plan (Exhibit F) shows the location of a medical service
office building located roughly central to the western half of the property. The site currently
is comprised of three (3) separate parcels (Exhibit K), as a condition of approval completion
of the proposed consolidation into one (1) parcel will be necessary. The proposed site
layout otherwise conforms to all applicable ordinance requirements. Parking surrounds
the building on all sides. Additional surface parking is located towards the northeast corner
of the property near the intersection of 11400 S. and State Street. There is an existing
vehicular access from the east that connects to State Street that will be utilized for this
project and is shared with the existing Toscano’s Restaurant located to the south of the
access drive. The required pedestrian access from the street to the building will be
provided to 11400 S. The main entry it oriented north and includes a canopy over a drop
off and pick up area in front. Smaller covered entrances exist on the east and west sides of
the building. To the south, a vehicular entry ramp leads down to sixteen (16) additional
parking stalls located under the building in a basement area (Exhibit H). Building
mechanical equipment is located south of the building and is screened with rock faced
walls and landscaping. A lawn area and picnic pavilion are located to the south of the
building as part of the required site amenities. Bicycle parking is provided on the east side
of the building, north of the picnic pavilion. Trash collection is planned for the northwest
corner of the property adjacent to the northbound I-15 off ramp.

Parking and circulation. According to the provided Site Plan (Exhibit F) and floor plans
(Exhibit H) there will be 184 parking stalls provided on-site. This total complies with
ordinance requirements. The underground parking area will contain 6 compact parking
stalls in order to preserve access to adjacent entrances to building mechanical, service, and
storage areas in front of these stalls. Pedestrian access will comply with ordinance
requirements and be constructed of colored concrete across the vehicular access drive and
will connect out to 11400 S. The main access drive to the south is proposed to be
constructed primarily within the existing access easement. To facilitate the necessary turn
radii for the access drive, the proposed site layout adjusts a small portion of the proposed
access drive outside of the easement area. As a condition of approval the property owner
will need to grant an access easement to the other adjacent properties for use of the
portions of the proposed access drive that will be outside the existing access easement.
Required cross access will be provided through the easements across the southern most

Architecture. The architectural elevation and floor plans (Exhibit H) show the proposed
exterior construction of a 4 story office building with a basement level including
underground parking. The exterior finish materials primarily consist of stone. The
proposed stone will have two finish types, a split face near the base of the structure and a
smooth or polished face in areas above that. Matching stone would be used to face the
mechanical enclosures, trash enclosure, and pavilion. Small amounts of stucco would be
utilized for cornice details near the roofline. The roofing material would be standing seam
metal in a light stone color. Windows near the ground or pedestrian level are required to
be transparent and the applicant has indicated that these windows will comply with
ordinance and has provided an applicable detail sample of the transparent windows
(Exhibit I). The proposal does not include any detail sample regarding tinting or mirroring of
windows above the first floor. The elevation drawings indicate that the glass will be a
specific brand of low-e glass that would have minimal tint or reflectivity. The color and
material sample boards (Exhibit I) provided by the applicant do not directly align with the
materials on the elevation drawings. As a condition of approval the applicant should
submit a revised material and color sample board that correctly aligns the labeling with the
colors and materials specified on the elevation drawings.

As proposed the height of the building is sixty-seven feet two-inches (67’ 2”) and exceeds
the maximum height in the zone of fifty-five feet (55’). The applicant has included a letter
requesting approval of a deviation for the additional height together with the site plan
application (Exhibit L). Additionally in that letter the architect has requested deviations
from the requirements to utilize a minimum of two (2) primary materials and three (3)
colors on each façade. With the most recent set of elevation drawings provided to staff the
proposal complies with the color requirement, but not with the minimum requirement to
utilize two (2) primary materials on each façade.

Architectural Design Standards Modification. When the application was initially submitted
applicable provisions in DCMC 9-11-070 and DCMC Section 9-22-030 allowed for deviations
from the maximum allowable height listed for the CI zone as well as from other
architectural design standards. After the application was submitted the City amended
these code sections and the current code would not permit the specific deviation from the
maximum height as requested with this application. This application and review are subject



Radnet Corporate Office Building                                                 App. # «JS_File_Number»
Site Plan Request                                         6
to the prior codes in effect at the time of application submittal. The following listed code
requirements reflect the actual requirements and findings applicable to the review and
approval of the deviations requested with this application.

DCMC Section 9-11-070 states that greater building height may be allowed in all
commercial zones, except the CN and TC zones, pursuant to the approval of a deviation by
the planning commission. Any deviation shall meet the following standards:

    1. The proposed height shall not have a material adverse effect upon the character of the
       area or the public health, safety and general welfare.
    2. The proposed height shall be constructed and arranged so as to be compatible with the
       use and development of neighboring properties with respect to scale and massing.
    3. The building will be designed to relate to the human scale and incorporate at least one of
       the following:
       a. Architectural detailing including on the ground floor to emphasize the pedestrian
           level of the building, including, but not limited to, intermediate cornice line, sign
           band, awnings or portico feature, change in building materials, and window shape.
       b. Include architectural detailing at the cornice level or accentuated building zones,
           when appropriate to the architectural style of the building.
       c. The roofline contains architectural features that give it a distinctive form or skyline, or
           the rooftop is designed for purposes such as rooftop gardens, common space for
           building occupants or the public, viewing platforms, shading or daylighting
           structures, renewable energy systems, and other similar uses.

Pertaining to the deviation request for additional building height under DCMC Section 9-11-
070 the architect stated that the building will not impact health, safety or welfare in the
area and will not adversely affect the character of the neighborhood. With respects to the
second criterion for approval the architect cited other large commercial developments on
neighboring properties and the shared access routes with adjacent developments as
evidence that the proposed height of the building would be compatible with neighboring
properties with respect to scale and massing. Staff also notes that an office building on the
neighboring property to the South of the subject property with a maximum height above
grade of sixty-two feet (62’) with average height of fifty-five feet (55’) was approved in 2022
but has not yet been constructed. With respect to the third criterion the architect indicated
that details at the main level are scaled to emphasize pedestrian interactions specifically
lower entries, covered walkways, a porte-cochere and a covered pavilion. This complies
with the requirement to incorporate at least one of the features listed in 9-11-070(A)(3).The
architect also pointed out in their request the contemporary architectural style of the
cornice details and the sloped roofline that provides a distinctive form consistent with the
architectural style. The Planning Commission will need to find that all standards for
granting the deviation for additional height have been met in order to grant the deviation.




Radnet Corporate Office Building                                           App. # «JS_File_Number»
Site Plan Request                                 7
DCMC Section 9-22-030 states that the Planning Commission may approve architectural
plans associated with development applications that deviate from the requirements of the
DCMC based on making at least three findings listed in DCMC Section 9-22-030(B):

    1. The project contains amenities such as pedestrian and bike connectivity in excess of what
        is required in the development code and site plan review.
    2. The overall percentage of dedicated public or private landscape and open space area
        exceeds the required amount by more than ten percent (10%).
    3. The project is a transit oriented development (TOD) and provides connectivity to a
        transportation facility.
    4. Traffic impacts on the neighborhood are lessened through programs, such as creative
        design, traffic calming measures, companywide carpool or transit pass programs.
    5. The project is an accredited LEED development.
    6. The variations are consistent with the purpose of this chapter and any applicable master
        plan or ordinance.
    7. The project is required to create a consistent and compatible design in cases which
        involve redeveloped buildings, additions to existing buildings, minor structures added to
        a site, or new buildings within a previously approved phased project.
    8. Additional landscape plant material is provided at least ten percent (10%) more than the
        minimum required, including additional planting beds, plants, trees or a combination
        thereof.
    9. The building design is a specific architectural style, such as contemporary or modern,
        which utilizes facade materials differently then prescribed in subsection 9-22-040F of this
        chapter and is designed by a licensed architect.
    10. The amount of primary materials used for a facade is at least ten percent (10%) greater
        than the minimum required amount.

In the request for deviation from the exterior primary material standards of DCMC chapter
9-22 the architect cites the transit oriented nature of the project being near major public
transportation routes as evidence that the project complies with criterion 3 in DCMC 9-22-
030(B). The site is approximately ½ mile from the nearest bus stop on the Jordan
Gateway/Lone Peak Parkway bus route and 0.8 miles from the Crescent View Trax station.
Staff notes that walkability to transit is typically defined as being within ½ mile, and TODs
also include other design elements that improve pedestrian access such as locating
buildings near the street. The path of travel for pedestrian access from the proposed
building to the nearest bus station crosses under the I-15 freeway, and although it includes
sufficient sidewalks and cross walks necessary to reach the nearest bus stop, presents a
number of navigational challenges and is inadequately maintained. In staff’s opinion, the
architect’s statements do not adequately support the claim that the project is a transit
oriented development for use as consideration of criterion 3 for deviation approval.

In response to criterion 6 the architect claims that the proposed variations are consistent
with Draper Master Plan and Zoning ordinances. While the architect was likely referring to



Radnet Corporate Office Building                                          App. # «JS_File_Number»
Site Plan Request                                8
the General Plan, there is not an applicable Master Plan for the property or area. The
architect did not provide additional details in their specific analysis on how the requested
variations were consistent with ordinance requirements, however, elsewhere in the letter
the architect does state that they feel the proposed “natural stone” masonry finish is
equally viable and attractive as a singular exterior finish to that of brick. The Planning
Commission may consider that statement in support of compliance with criterion 6.

In support of criterion 9, the architect does state that the building is designed by a licensed
architect in a contemporary style. No details were specified on how the design utilized
façade materials differently than prescribed in 9-22-040(F).

The architect has provided calculations of the amount of primary materials planned for
each side of the building on the elevation drawings (Exhibit H). The amounts exceed the
minimum required amount of 75% by more than 10% and the design of all exterior façades
does comply with criterion 10.

The Planning Commission will need to find that at least three (3) criteria from the list in 9-
22-030(B) have been met in order to grant the deviation to allow for use of only one (1)
primary material.

Lighting. The lighting plans (Exhibit J) shows the location of exterior lights and their
illumination readings across the site both for business hours and after-hours operation.
The plans are generally compliant with ordinance, however staff noted that the calculation
tables omitted the required calculation regarding the ratio between maximum and average
illumination and that the required average illumination was mislabeled as max average. As
a condition of approval staff recommends that the updated calculation table be provided
as part of revised plans to staff for review and approval. The plans do call out a maximum
twenty feet (20’) in height for the light poles in the parking areas which does comply with
ordinance. No color for the light poles was specified, per ordinance black poles will be
required as another color has not been specified.

Fencing. Fencing for the property consists of the existing chain link fence installed by UDOT
along the property line adjacent to the northbound I-15 freeway off ramp, and a proposed
four foot (4’) tall chain link fence located behind a retaining wall on the west and north of
the property (Exhibit F). The chain link fence is necessary for maintaining site safety near
the retaining wall as the retaining wall would measure nine feet (9’) in height at its tallest
point.

Criteria For Approval.
The criteria for review and potential approval of the deviations for additional height and
façade materials and colors are listed above in the Architectural Design Standards
Modification section of this report.

The criteria for review and potential approval of a Site Plan request is found in Sections 9-5-
090(E) of the DCMC. This section depicts the standard of review for such requests as:

E. Standards For Approval: The following standards shall apply to the approval of a site
   plan:
   1. The entire site shall be developed at one time unless a phased development plan is
      approved.
   2. A site plan shall conform to applicable standards set forth in this title, including but
      not limited to, building heights, setbacks, access points, parking, landscaping, and
      building materials.
   3. The proposed development plans meet the intent, goals, and objectives of the
      general plan and the purpose of the zone district in which the site is located.

       utilities concerns.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission review the request, receive public
comment, and make a decision based on the findings listed below and the criteria for
approval, or denial, as listed within the staff report.

If the Planning Commission decides to approve the site plan request, staff recommends
they include the following conditions of approval:

    1. That all requirements of the Draper City Engineering, Public Works, Building,
       Planning, and Fire Divisions are satisfied throughout the development of the site

         and the construction of all buildings on the site, including permitting.
    2.   That all requirements of the geotechnical report are satisfied throughout the
         development of the site and the construction of all buildings on the site.
    3.   That the applicant resolve issues regarding the submittal of the required
         stormwater maintenance plan and agreement and execute the agreement as part of
         the Land Disturbance Permit process.
    4.   That consolidation of the property into a single parcel be completed prior to staff
         giving final approval to the site plan application.
    5.   That revised landscaping plans be submitted to planning staff for review and
         approval that show the existing landscaping as proposed with the addition of the
         required shrubs and irrigation added to the landscape planter islands.
    6.   That the proposed additional access easements across the proposed access drive to
         the South be granted for use by the adjoining properties, be recorded on the
         property with the County Recorder, and that the applicant provide copies of the
         recorded deed documents to planning staff prior to receiving final approval.
    7.   That revised color and material sample boards that align with the colors and
         materials specified on the elevation drawings be provided to planning staff for
         review and approval.
    8.   That revised lighting plans with the corrections noted in the staff report be provided

Deviation Request from DCMC Section 9-11-070 – Increased Height
The findings for approval as are follows:

    1. The proposed height will not have a material adverse effect upon the character of
       the area or the public health, safety and general welfare.
    2. The proposed construction and arrangement of the building height is compatible
       with the use and development of neighboring properties with respect to scale and
       massing.
    3. The building is designed to relate to the human scale and incorporates at least one
       of the following:
       a. Architectural detailing including on the ground floor to emphasize the
           pedestrian level of the building.
       b. Architectural detailing at the cornice level or accentuated building zones.
       c. Roofline architectural features that give it a distinctive form or skyline.

The findings for denial as are follows:

    1. The proposed height will have a material adverse effect upon the character of the
       area or the public health, safety and general welfare.
    2. The proposed construction and arrangement of the building height is not
       compatible with the use and development of neighboring properties with respect to
       scale and massing.

Site Plan
The findings for approval as are follows:

    1. The site plan reflects the full development of the property.
    2. The site plan with approval of the deviation requests conforms to applicable
       standards set forth in ordinance, including but not limited to, building heights,
       setbacks, access points, parking, landscaping, and building materials.
    3. The proposed development plans meet the intent, goals, and objectives of the
       general plan and the purpose of the CI zoning district in which the site is located.
    4. The public facilities and services in the area are adequate to support the subject
       development, as required by engineering standards and specifications.
    5. The proposed development plans will comply with the engineering standards found
       in Titles 7, 8, 11, 12, 16, and 18 of the Draper City Municipal Code, including traffic,
       storm water drainage, and utilities concerns.

The findings for denial as are follows:

    1. The one or more of the deviation requests were denied and the site plan does not
       conform to applicable standards set forth in ordinance without approval of the
       deviation requests.
    2. The proposed development plans do not meet the intent, goals, and objectives of
       the general plan and the purpose of the CI zoning district in which the site is located.

                                 DEPARTMENT REVIEWS

REVIEWS ARE NOT MEANT TO BE AN ALL INCLUSIVE LIST OF POSSIBLE COMMENTS OR
CONDITIONS.

Planning Division Review.

   1. No additional comments.

Engineering and Public Works Divisions Review.

   1. We have reviewed the Site Plan application for the subject project for compliance to
      the Draper City Municipal Code (DCMC). Accordingly, we have included the following
      comments for your consideration:

       CONDITIONALLY MEETS REQUIREMENTS

       General Comments:
       a. Stormwater Maintenance Plan and Agreement are now required for every
          private storm drainage system, per DCMC 16-2-170. Submission of the
          maintenance plan is now required prior to site approval. The maintenance
          agreement is a condition of approval; it is required to be recorded and returned
          to the city prior to issuance of the Land Disturbance Permit for construction of
          the site. Comment will be a condition of approval to resolve and execute agreement
          as part of the Land Disturbance Permit process.
       b. Access permit from UDOT is required. Access Updated access permit will be a
          condition of approval and is required prior to issuance of a Land Disturbance Permit.
       c. Retaining walls are to comply with DCMC 9-27-085. Retaining walls are not
          reviewed or approved with this review and approval process. Comment is
          informational. No additional action required prior to site plan approval.
       d. Once site plan has been approved, a Land Disturbance Permit is required prior
          to construction activities onsite. Permit is obtained through the Engineering
          Division and is required prior to Building Permit issuance. Comment is
          informational. No additional action required prior to site plan approval.
       e. Any work in the public right-of-way will require an Encroachment Permit
          obtained through the Engineering Division. Comment is informational. No
          additional action required prior to site plan approval.

Building Division Review.

   1. No additional comments.
Geotechnical and Geologic Hazards Review.

   1. No additional comments.

Fire Division Review.

   1. Engineer’s water supply analysis required. The design team will provide to the
       Draper City Fire Marshal an engineer’s water supply analysis.
   2. Fire department access is required.
   3. Compliance with IFC Section 3310 for fire fighting access during construction is
       required.
   4. Compliance with IFC chapter 33 fire safety during construction and demolition is
       required.
   5. Fire Hydrants are required. A minimum of 4 hydrants, are required.
   6. All Hydrants and temporary access to the site shall be installed and approved by the
       Fire Department prior to the issuance of any building permits.
   7. No combustible construction shall be allowed prior to hydrant installation and
       testing by water purveyor. All hydrants must be operational prior to any
       combustible elements being received or delivered on the building site.
   8. Fire sprinklers are required. Deferred submittal for a NFPA 13 fire sprinkler system
       to be sent to Fire Marshal. Plans must be stamped by a NICET level III or better in
       Auto Sprinkler Layout. Hydrant required within 100 feet of the FDC. FDC is required
       to have KNOX locking Caps. All fire protection plans require 3rd party review prior to
       submittal to the Draper Fire Department.
   9. Fire Department Connection required. Must be located to avoid interference with
       nearby objects.
   10. The building will be required to have standpipes.
   11. Installation of a fire alarm system is required. Deferred submittal to be sent to the
       Fire Marshal. Plans must be stamped by a NICET level III or better fire alarm system.
       All fire alarm plans required 3rd party review prior to submittal to the Draper Fire
       Department.
   12. UL300 system required. Deferred submittal to be sent to the Fire Marshal for the
       Ansul UL300 wet chemical kitchen hood system. A construction permit is required
       from the fire department.
   13. Emergency Responder Radio Coverage is required in accordance with the IFC 510.
   14. Two way communication required per Section 1009.8 in the 2018 IFC.
   15. KNOX Boxes are required to be mounted to exterior walls at a height of 5 feet to the
       top of the box, near the main entrance and the door servicing the exterior access to
       the fire sprinkler riser room.
   16. 2A-10BC Fire Extinguishers are required. Must be placed at least every 75 feet of
       travel. May not be mounted so that the top is more than five feet (5’) above the
       floor.
17. Visible addressing is required. Building shall have approved address numbers
    plainly legible and visible from the street fronting the property. These number shall
    contrast with their background.
18. Plan approval or review shall not, be construed to relieve from or lessen the
    responsibility of any person designing, owning, operating or controlling any
    building. Damages to persons or property caused by defects, fire, improper
    installation, or other emergency conditions that occur in or on the building property
    shall not hold the Draper City Fire Department as assuming any liability.

DEVIATION REQUEST:
At the request of the property owner, we request approval for deviations in certain elements that vary from
standards recommended in the Draper City Municipal Code. This project was submitted for Site Design Review
under the previous version of Draper Ordinance 9-11-070 and is eligible for consideration under those
regulations, as well as current requirements.

   1)         Requirement for maximum height of 45 feet.
              As the design has developed, the actual building height for the proposed building is 67’-2” as
              measured per Draper City Building Design Guidelines, Zoning Ordinance 9-22-040. The true
              measurement is exaggerated due to sloping topography, though still above 45 feet.

              The site is immediately East of Interstate highway I-15, bounded by 11400 S to the north and State
              Street to the east, at the border between Draper and Sandy. Surrounding properties on all sides are
              commercial and retail shopping centers with wide parking lots (i.e., Scheel’s, Best Buy, Zurcher’s in
              the neighborhood).

              •   The increased height will not impact health, safety or welfare in the area and will not adversely
                  affect the character of the neighborhood. (9-11-070 #A1)

              •   This proposed medical and professional office building is designed to be compatible with other
                  large commercial developments on neighboring properties, including shared access routes with
                  adjacent developments. (9-11-070 #A2)

              •   Architectural details at the main level are scaled to emphasize pedestrian interaction, including
                  lower entries, covered walkways, porte cochere and a covered pavilion. Windows provide
                  additional transparency at the pedestrian level. Cornice details and glass façade are consistent
                  with Contemporary architectural style. Sloped roofline and wide overhangs provide a distinctive
                  form consistent with architectural style and purpose. Continuous glass curtainwalls and brace-
                  frame construction provide expansive views and natural lighting deep into the building on all
                  sides. (9-11-070 #A3)




920 E. 800 North, Suite 201, Orem, UT 84097            Phone: 801.377.6303           www.harris-architecture.com
Page 1 of 3 .
           The proposed project seeks to be consistent with on-going developments in a commercial
           neighborhood that crosses City boundaries, and this proposal is consistent with current
           developments on adjacent properties.

           Please consider our Deviation Request regarding additional height and join in the development of
           this community. We believe it will provide incentive and encouragement for additional
           development as the community continues to thrive.


   2)      Requirement for minimum of 2 primary materials and 3 colors.
           The proposed building has one primary exterior finish material – natural granite stone. The
           ordinance allows “brick” as a single exterior material – without deviation – but that is the only
           prescribed exception. We feel that the proposed “natural stone” masonry finish is equally viable
           and attractive as a singular exterior finish.

           Further, the stone will have a “split-faced” finish wainscot below with a smooth “honed” finish
           above, which adds visual variety and texture – even with granite from the same quarry. From any
           perspective, the proposed building will not appear monolithic or monochromatic. Glass is a major
           component in the visual impact of the building, as well as the contemporary sloped roof design.

           •   The project is ‘transit oriented.’ Located at the intersection of I-15 and 114 South, the project is
               near major public transportation routes - approximately ½ mile from bus routes along Jordan
               Gateway, and less than one mile (0.8 mi.) from the Crescent View light rail station. (9-22-030
               #B3)

           •   The proposed variations are consistent with Draper Master Plan and Zoning Ordinances. (9-22-
               030 #B6)

           •   The proposed project is designed by a licensed Architect in a contemporary style with glass
               facades, natural stone and softened neutral colors, carefully selected to blend with surrounding
               mountain views and high-desert landscaping. (9-22-030 #B9) ***

           •   Primary materials cover 92.2% (overall) of the exterior facade area, which is more than 10%
               greater than the minimum required amount (75%).
               (Primary material, all sides - N: 92.3%, S:93.0%, E:90.7%, W:91.8%) (9-22-030 #B10)

           Please consider our Deviation Request regarding distribution of Primary and Secondary materials
           and the number of material colors.


We believe this development is consistent with the City of Draper’s intent to improve our city and this
neighborhood, in particular. We seek support and acceptance from the City of Draper for components of the
proposed project that may deviate from Draper Ordinance.
